Definition: Whether an official government web portal or mobile application exists where taxpayers can file tax returns and pay taxes online with direct e-payment capability linked to instant payment system.
Comments: No evidence found of a comprehensive national online tax e-filing portal in Guinea; searches focused on Guinea tax e-filing/portal and revenue authority e-services returned evidence of specific digital payment initiatives (e.g., vehicle tax via Orange Money; Trésor Pay for fees) but not an end-to-end tax portal with filing + payment. Therefore marked unknown/NA.

revision_notes: Light check surfaced a clearly authoritative source, so the row was escalated to the full path. The Direction Nationale des Impôts (DNI) operates the eTax portal (etax.gov.gn), officially launched 14 September 2020, which provides both télédéclaration (online filing) and télépaiement (online e-payment) directly linked to a taxpayer's registered bank account. The system was upgraded (SAFIG2) in 2024 to add e-invoicing for VAT. Payment is routed through partner banks rather than through the country's forthcoming instant payment system (SPI), which is separately still under development, so the specific 'linked to instant payment system' element of the definition is only partially met; the core filing-plus-payment portal functionality is confirmed. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 4 (Yes).
revised_comments: Guinea operates the eTax portal (etax.gov.gn), run by the Direction Nationale des Impôts, which allows taxpayers to file tax declarations and pay taxes online (télédéclaration and télépaiement). Launched in September 2020, the portal requires taxpayers to register a bank account, obtain a payment authorisation validated by their bank, and then make e-payments directly through the portal without needing to visit a tax office or bank counter. In 2024 the DNI upgraded the underlying system (SAFIG2), adding features such as electronic VAT invoicing. Online payment currently operates via linked bank accounts rather than through the national instant payment system, which remains under separate development.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No credible primary-source evidence found that Guinea’s Law L/2016/037/AN (cybersecurity & personal data protection) mandates breach notification to regulators and/or affected individuals; searched the law’s official publication page and related summaries for “notification/notify/violation” requirements but did not find a clear mandatory breach notification obligation in accessible primary sources ([ANSSI Guinée – Loi L/2016/037/AN](https://anssi.gov.gn/?nproject=loi-l037-2016-relative-a-la-cybersecurite-et-la-protection-des-donnees-a-caractere-personnel)).
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Light check surfaced a clearly authoritative, very recent source, so the row was escalated to the full path. A presidential decree read on national television on 21 May 2026 establishes a mandatory cybersecurity audit, certification and incident-notification regime for all entities conducting electronic transactions in Guinea, under the Autorité de Régulation des Postes et Télécommunications (ARPT). It mandates a 24-hour initial alert and a 72-hour detailed report to ARPT for incidents affecting a significant number of users. This supplements the pre-existing Law L/2016/037/AN. Recalculated from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Mandatory).
revised_comments: A presidential decree announced on 21 May 2026 establishes a mandatory cybersecurity audit, certification and incident-notification regime for all public and private entities conducting electronic transactions in Guinea, under the supervision of the Autorité de Régulation des Postes et Télécommunications (ARPT). Entities must report any major cybersecurity incident or significant system change; where an incident affects a large number of users, an initial alert must be sent to ARPT within 24 hours, followed by a detailed report within 72 hours. Security audits are mandatory every three years (more frequently for critical or sensitive infrastructure), and foreign companies serving Guinean residents must also comply. This builds on the pre-existing Law L/2016/037/AN on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection, which established the Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL) as the data protection authority.

Comments: No credible public evidence found of independent public audits/reviews specific to Guinea’s national payment systems (RTGS/ACH/SPI) or their operators; searches returned general corporate audits (e.g., MTN Group) but not payment-system operator audits relevant to Guinea’s infrastructure governance. revision_notes: Light check surfaced two relevant but conflicting signals, so the row was escalated to the full path; evidence remains inconclusive and is flagged for human review rather than a scored change. (1) BCRG publishes its own externally audited annual financial statements (IFRS auditor's report and commissaire aux comptes report, 2019-2023), which are institutional financial audits of the central bank rather than payment-system-specific security/operational audits. (2) A May 2026 presidential decree makes third-party security audits mandatory every three years for electronic-transaction operators (which would include payment service providers), but explicitly requires that audit reports remain strictly confidential. These point in different directions — one public, one confidential by law — and neither directly confirms whether Guinea's payment-system infrastructure specifically (RTGS/ACH/SPI) undergoes public independent audits. Value code left unchanged pending human review.
revised_comments: Evidence on independent audits of Guinea's payment system infrastructure specifically is mixed and inconclusive. The BCRG publishes externally audited annual financial statements for the institution as a whole (auditeur contractuel IFRS report and commissaire aux comptes report), but these cover the central bank's overall accounts rather than payment-system security or operations specifically. Separately, a May 2026 presidential decree mandates security audits every three years for entities conducting electronic transactions, supervised by the telecoms regulator ARPT, but requires that the resulting audit reports remain confidential.
